name: Emirates SkyCargo
description: The 2023 Emirates livery on the 777 freighters: white with no windows, the rippled flag on the fin with its red band sweeping down the rear fuselage; 'Emirates' in gold over the forward fuselage underlined with a thin gold rule, 'SkyCargo' in red under its end, the Arabic title in gold just ahead of the wing, red belly panel with 'Emirates'.

sources.title: Emirates unveils new signature livery for its fleet (press release, 16 March 2023; cited by Wikipedia)
sources.note: A flowing, 3D UAE flag on the tail; red wingtips with the logo in white calligraphy, the flag's colors on their inner faces. Read through Wikipedia's 'Livery' section.

logos.description: The Emirates logo: the name in Arabic calligraphy (Diwani-style), a compact knot of strokes a little taller than wide, about half the cowling's height, in gold on the outboard side of each cowling.
The calligraphy logo, small, in white on the red winglet's outer face.

titles.style: The Emirates wordmark in gold: a bold old-style serif, mixed case, over the forward fuselage.
'SkyCargo' in red, one word with a capital C, a semi-bold upright serif, right-aligned under the end of 'Emirates'.
'Al Emarat' in gold Arabic calligraphy, aft of 'Emirates' just ahead of the wing root (often hidden by the wing in photos).
The wordmark in white on the red belly panel, reading along the fuselage.

notes: The passenger 2023 scheme with the freighter titles: 'Emirates' moves down and forward, a thin gold rule runs under it, 'SkyCargo' in red under its tail end, the Arabic sits aft. Measured on A6-EWK (right side, 2026-04-01; nose to the right, the titles read the same on both sides, as A6-EWQ's left side shows). New 777Fs (A6-EW*) arrive in it and older ones are being repainted (A6-EFN, EFV, EFX and EFZ wear it in 2026 photos); the rest still wear the 1999 flag scheme with the same titles (cargo-1999). The fin, red sweep and belly panel are the passenger file's, which these photos agree with. The six wet-leased 747-400Fs fly in their operators' colors and are not tagged. Belly title 'Emirates' as on the passenger aircraft, seen only obliquely on A6-EWQ. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on A6-EWK (777F): 'Emirates' (x 0.100 to 0.309), 'SkyCargo' (0.102 to 0.177) and the red sweep (leaving the crown about x 0.82 to 0.85, its point about x 0.70, y -0.54) agree with the drawing within the photo's perspective; the Arabic title's aft end is behind the wing, so its length (0.077) is the 2023 scheme's 4.9 m on the A350 taken onto the 777F (low). The red sweep is smooth.
history: Emirates SkyCargo's freighters took the 2023 livery from 2024-2025 (new deliveries and repaints); it replaces the 1999 flag-tail cargo scheme (cargo-1999), still worn by about half the 777Fs in late 2026.
